summary: Contestants demonstrate a basic understanding of financial literacy by completing an objective and application-based test. The event is open to any middle level contestant and includes topics such as budgeting, credit management, and ethical financial decision-making.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than sixty (60) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non -electronic written reference materials
Cordless calculator: electronic devices will be monitored according to ACT standards
competencies: Develop and manage a comprehensive personal financial plan using tools for budgeting, forecasting, and goal tracking
Demonstrate understanding of digital payment systems, credit management, and fraud prevention
Analyze and calculate interest, debt, and credit impacts using financial tools to support informed decision-making
Solve financial problems using basic mathematical operations
Differentiate between responsible and irresponsible financial decisions
Demonstrate an understanding of basic personal banking
Apply ethical decision-making and compliance standards in finance, including the understanding of consequences to financial decisions
Analyze opportunity cost in career, education, and investment decisions
Evaluate saving, investing, opportunity cost, and lifestyle choices to align financial decisions with long-term goals
judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
No equipment, supplies, or materials other than those specified for an event will be allowed in the testing area
Previous Business Professionals of America tests (handwritten, photocopied, or keyed) may not be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.
Competitors who violate calculator rule will be disqualified.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level contestant may enter this application event.
